messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Torres <samuel.torres@greenleaf.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput fit & safety cushion for GreenLeaf Dedicated - token horizon planning

Hi Samuel —

Great to meet on the call last week. To put together a solid Dedicated proposal (sizing + safety cushion) we need a few quick inputs so our capacity model maps cleanly to your SLOs and peak behaviour. Can you confirm the numbers below where possible? If you have a short export, that helps (CSV or BigQuery link).

Quick ask:
- Avg requests per second (sustained) and typical daily peak (req/s and duration).
- Average tokens per request (or distribution: median/95th).
- P95 latency target we should design to (ms) and whether streaming output is used.
- % of requests that must use the high-quality 70B model vs a cheaper 13B equivalent.
- Any blackout windows or known seasonal peaks (e.g., marketing events, Black Friday multiples).

Our baseline modelling assumptions we'll use unless you flag otherwise:
- 13B quantized (8-bit/4-bit kernel) ≈ 5,000 tokens/sec per A100-class GPU (sustained, small-batch optimized).
- 70B quantized on H100-ish ≈ 800 tokens/sec per GPU (higher memory / slower throughput).
- We'll size to meet P95 latency with an ops-friendly headroom multiplier (default 1.5x) and propose an autoscaling burst band for short spikes.

If you can send a quick CSV of 7 days of traffic, I'll run the numbers and put a slab proposal + burst plan together.

Thanks —
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks, attaching a short export (greenleaf_usage_q2.csv). Notes inline:

- Avg sustained: ~12 req/s (measured over last 30 days).
- Typical avg tokens/request: 320–380 (median 345). For safety use 350 tokens as a representative mean.
- Daily peak: usually 15:00–15:20 PST window; observed short peaks up to ~220 req/s (15 minute burst), but sustained peaks for ~1 hour top out at ~120 req/s.
- P95 target: 800 ms (user-facing streaming UI; sub-1s is critical).
- Quality split: today all traffic is routed to a high-quality 70B model. Long-term we'd like to move ~80% to a lower-cost 13B where quality is acceptable and keep 20% on 70B for high-touch users.
- Seasonality: marketing campaigns (quarterly) can increase baseline by ~2–3x for 48–72 hours.

Can you sketch a conservative slab (# reserved GPUs), burst ceiling, and what that means for day tokens and cost? Happy to run a pilot.

Samuel Torres
Head of Infrastructure, GreenLeaf AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: GreenLeaf numbers + ask — capacity calc (please run quick model)

Kimberly / Ben / Marcus — forwarding GreenLeaf numbers (see attachment). Quick calc notes below, want to validate before I reply with a formal slab proposal.

Customer inputs used: avg req/s = 12, avg tokens = 350, peak burst = 220 req/s for 15 min, 1hr sustained peaks ~120 req/s, P95 target = 800 ms, quality split target 80% on 13B / 20% on 70B in steady-state. Seasonal x3 multiplier for campaign windows.

Assumptions for our throughput model:
- 13B quantized on A100-class GPU: conservative throughput = 5,000 tokens/sec per GPU (sustained, continuous batching, KV cache benefits applied).
- 70B quantized on H100-class GPU: conservative throughput = 800 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Autoscaling adds GPUs in 10-20% increments with ~30s warmup (with pre-warmed KV cache can be faster).
- Safety multiplier (ops headroom) = 1.5x for sizing reserved capacity (to hit P95 under medium spikes).

Compute token load:
- Avg sustained token/sec = 12 req/s * 350 tok = 4,200 tokens/sec.
- Peak burst token/sec = 220 * 350 = 77,000 tokens/sec (15-min window).
- 1hr sustained peak token/sec = 120 * 350 = 42,000 tokens/sec.

Split plan (steady-state 80/20):
- Steady-state tokens/sec to 13B = 0.8 * 4,200 = 3,360 tok/sec.
- Steady-state tokens/sec to 70B = 0.2 * 4,200 = 840 tok/sec.

GPU count (raw, before headroom):
- 13B GPUs required = ceil(3,360 / 5,000) = 1 GPU (but realistically need at least 2 for redundancy and SLO).
- 70B GPUs required = ceil(840 / 800) = 2 GPUs.

Now apply headroom and peak handling:
- Apply 1.5x headroom to steady-state => reserved 13B capacity target = 1 * 1.5 = 1.5 => round up to 2 GPUs reserved for 13B.
- Reserved 70B capacity target = 2 * 1.5 = 3 GPUs reserved for 70B.

Peak burst handling (77k tok/sec):
- If we route the burst majority to 13B (best-effort quality tradeoff), tokens/sec per A100=5,000 -> to cover 77k we'd need 16 GPUs raw. If 70B handles only 20% of requests during burst, then burst load on 13B ~61.6k tok/sec -> 13B GPUs needed ~13 (61.6k / 5k).
- We can cover peaks with autoscaling: reserved baseline 2 x 13B + 3 x 70B, autoscale up to ~16 x 13B (or equivalent H100s) for short windows.

Day tokens capacity (reserved 13B baseline):
- Reserved 13B capacity tokens/day = 2 GPUs * 5,000 tok/sec * 86,400 sec = 864M tokens/day (0.864 billion).
- With autoscale and burst retention we can sustain much larger day totals; for capacity planning we express entitlement as reserved baseline + burst runway. GreenLeaf asked about 100M tokens/day — our baseline covers that easily.

Operational recommendation:
- Proposal: Reserved slab = 2 x A100 (13B quantized) + 3 x H100 (70B quantized) with autoscaling policy to add up to +14 A100s (for 16 total) during sustained spikes; burst policy: step-up increments of 4 GPUs with fast pre-warm for KV cache.
- Rationale: minimizes cost by serving most traffic on cheap 13B while keeping 70B available for high-touch flows. Meets p95=800ms target in normal and moderate spikes; large 15-min spikes are handled through autoscale.
- Canary plan: 30-day pilot with canary routing (10% traffic to new slab for 48 hours) then full cutover. Include deployment playbook for telemetry and rollback.

Ben / Marcus — please sanity-check the tokens/sec per GPU numbers and latency mapping (I used our conservative kernels). If you agree I'll send this back to Samuel + a draft estimate.

Thanks —
Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Torres <samuel.torres@greenleaf.ai>, procurement <procurement@greenleaf.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed Dedicated slab + burst runway for GreenLeaf (short summary + next steps)

Samuel — thanks for the quick data. Attached is a concise estimate (Redwood_estimate_v2.pdf) and the sizing summary below. High level first, then an ops playbook.

Sizing summary (conservative):
- Reserved slab: 2 x A100 (primary: 13B quantized) + 3 x H100 (high-quality 70B)
- Autoscale burst ceiling: up to 16 x A100 equivalents for short spikes (15–60 min); policy: step +4 GPUs every 30s with pre-warm tier.
- Headroom factor: 1.5x applied to steady-state to preserve P95=800ms under medium spikes.
- Day token throughput (reserved baseline): ~864M tokens/day on 13B reserved slab. With autoscale headroom available for burst windows (handles multi-billion token days during campaigns).

Why this approach:
- Cost efficiency: Most traffic on 13B quantized gives good latency and much higher tokens/sec per GPU.
- Quality guardrail: 3 H100-backed 70B workers reserved for premium flows.
- Safety: 1.5x headroom and autoscale for 15-min bursts means user-facing p95 is preserved without overcommitting long-term.

Next steps / mutual action plan:
1) GreenLeaf: sign pilot SOW + provide 7 days of live telemetry for canary. (Procurement looped on this thread.)
2) Redwood: provision pilot slab (2A100 + 3H100) in dedicated pool, configure routing/weighting (80/20), enable tracing & token-level billing.
3) 48–72 hour canary with 10% traffic -> validate p95, tail latencies, KV cache hit rates.
4) If canary good -> commit to monthly reserved slab with burst ceiling and SLA addendum covering the autoscale behavior.

Cost estimate preview: monthly reserved slab + burst buffer estimate attached. Procurement — if you want, I can convert to a redlined Term Sheet and include a 60-day ramp discount.

Attachments: Redwood_estimate_v2.pdf (pricing + slab terms)

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow to walk the numbers with your infra team.

Best —
